optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Search Algorithm Engineer, Financial Reporting System

professionalSummary.text: Senior offline evaluation engineer with extensive experience developing and deploying ranking models for a financial reporting search service.
professionalSummary.witness: Developed and evaluated ranking models for the reporting system's search service offline against the labelled query set (about 3,400 finance queries), improving offline nDCG in three consecutive model iterations.

experienceHighlights.text: Built an offline evaluation harness and replay tool that scores ranking models against logged production queries.
experienceHighlights.witness: Built the offline evaluation harness and the replay tool that scores a ranking model against logged queries copied from the production index into the development cluster.

experienceHighlights.text: Coordinated releases with the platform team, ensuring smooth deployment of ranking changes to production search service.
experienceHighlights.witness: Coordinated releases with the platform team through the release review; ranking changes were deployed to the production search service by the platform team, and the live relevance dashboards were owned and monitored by the platform's search operations engineer.

experienceHighlights.text: Authored comprehensive model cards detailing training queries, offline metrics, known limitations, and hand‑over notes for each ranking iteration.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote the model card for each ranking iteration, listing the training queries, the offline metrics and the known limitation that document-type boosts were tuned only on logged queries, plus the hand-over notes for the platform team.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Delivered an offline evaluation report and replay tool README as part of the third ranking iteration, including development cluster job identifiers for verification.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the offline evaluation report for the third ranking iteration and the replay tool README, with the development cluster's job identifiers as a verification trail.

They do not provide explicit evidence of deploying ranking changes to production, operating production relevance monitoring, running live‑traffic experiments, coordinating releases with finance‑user teams, or documenting hand‑over conditions for each release.
